title: Paris Approach to Orthopedic Manual Therapy

hook.en: A step-by-step orthopedic examination that decides first whether a joint needs mobilizing, stabilizing or something else, then treats and retests.
hook.ur: Paris approach ek systematic orthopedic examination framework hai: pehle history aur movement check, phir problem ki classification, us ke mutabiq treatment aur dobara test.

goal.en: By the end, you'll know what Paris Approach to Orthopedic Manual Therapy is, when it's safe and useful, how to apply it step by step — and how to prove it worked. (4 checks along the way.)
goal.ur: End tak aap jaan jayenge ke Paris Approach to Orthopedic Manual Therapy kya hai, kab safe aur faida-mand hai, qadam ba qadam kaise apply hoti hai — aur kaise prove karein ke kaam kiya. (Raste mein 4 checks.)

text.en: The Paris approach, associated with Stanley Paris, is a framework for orthopedic manual therapy. You examine in a set order, classify the problem (for example hypomobile, hypermobile or not mechanical), choose joint-specific treatment, and teach exercises for lasting change.
text.ur: Stanley Paris se associated yeh framework orthopedic manual therapy mein examination ko ek munazzam order mein rakhta hai. Problem ko classify karke, misal ke taur par hypomobile, hypermobile ya non-mechanical, joint-specific treatment aur long-term change ke liye exercises choose ki jati hain.

simpler.en: A step-by-step orthopedic examination that decides first whether a joint needs mobilizing, stabilizing or something else, then treats and retests.
simpler.ur: Paris approach ek systematic orthopedic examination framework hai: pehle history aur movement check, phir problem ki classification, us ke mutabiq treatment aur dobara test.

text.en: Like a mechanic who diagnoses with a checklist before touching any bolt. The checking is the skill; the spanner comes later.
text.ur: Yeh mechanic ki tarah hai jo bolt chhoone se pehle checklist se problem diagnose karta hai. Asal skill checking mein hai; spanner baad mein aata hai.

text.en:
Three ideas carry this whole technique:
**1.** Examine before you treat: history, observation, active and passive movement, joint-play and neurological checks, in a consistent order.
**2.** Treat according to the finding: stiff joints may be mobilized, loose joints need stabilizing exercise.
**3.** Retest the functional problem and build active rehabilitation around it.
text.ur: Treatment se pehle history, observation, active/passive movement, joint play aur neurological checks karein. Stiff joint ko mobilization ki zaroorat ho sakti hai, jabke loose joint ko stabilizing exercise chahiye ho sakti hai. Functional problem ko retest karke active rehabilitation banayein.

question.en: Vocabulary first — clinicians use this word a lot. What does **Hypomobile** mean?
question.ur: Pehle vocabulary — clinicians yeh lafz bohat use karte hain. **Hypomobile** ka matlab kya hai?

text.en: A joint moving more than expected; usually needs stability, not stretching.
text.ur: A joint moving more than expected; usually needs stability, not stretching.

text.en:
So when does **Paris Approach to Orthopedic Manual Therapy** make sense?
• Joint or spine problems where you need a clear reason for choosing manual therapy.
• Teaching and learning systematic examination.
text.ur: Joint ya spine problems mein jab manual therapy choose karne ki clear wajah chahiye, aur systematic examination sikhane ke liye. Red flags hon to pehle medical review karein. Isay rigid recipe na banayein; sequence patient ki zaroorat ke liye hai.

text.en:
And just as important — when you should NOT use it, or should stop:
• When red flags need medical review first.
• As a rigid recipe: the order serves the patient, not the other way round.
**Stop rule:** Avoid forceful mobilization with instability, suspected fracture, infection, significant neurologic deficit or unexplained serious symptoms.
text.ur:
Utna hi zaroori — kab yeh technique NAHI karni, ya kab ruk jana hai:
• When red flags need medical review first.
• As a rigid recipe: the order serves the patient, not the other way round.
**Stop rule:** Avoid forceful mobilization with instability, suspected fracture, infection, significant neurologic deficit or unexplained serious symptoms.

title.en: How to do it — 6 steps, each with its reason
title.ur: Kaise karein — 6 qadam, har ek ki wajah ke saath

steps.title: Listen and screen
steps.detail: Take the history and rule out red flags.

steps.title: Observe and test active movement
steps.detail: Watch the movement and note where pain or limitation occurs.

steps.title: Test passive movement and joint play
steps.detail: Check range, end-feel and small glides, comparing sides.

steps.title: Check nerves, muscles and neighbouring joints
steps.detail: The problem may come from elsewhere.

steps.title: Classify and choose
steps.detail: Stiff joint: consider mobilization. Loose joint: stabilize. Unclear: refer or gather more data.

steps.title: Treat, retest and teach
steps.detail: Apply the treatment, retest the movement, and give exercises.

beats.ur:
1. History lein aur red flags screen karein.
2. Active movement observe karke pain aur limitation note karein.
3. Passive movement aur joint play, range, end-feel aur small glides assess karein.
4. Nerves, muscles aur nearby joints check karein.
5. Findings classify karein: stiffness mein mobilization consider ho sakti hai; laxity mein stabilization; unclear case mein aur data ya referral.
6. Treatment ke baad retest karein aur exercise sikhayein.

text.en: How much? No fixed dose. Dose follows the technique you choose (for example mobilization grades) and the patient's irritability.

beats.patient: Daniel, 55, architect, shoulder stiffness for weeks.
beats.assessment: Active and passive elevation are both limited with a firm end-feel; the glide of the joint is reduced; the neck and nerves are clear.
beats.treatment: A hypomobile pattern is identified, so joint mobilization and stretching are chosen, plus home exercises.
beats.reassess: Elevation improves and he returns to lifting tasks. Had the examination shown a loose joint, stabilizing exercises would have been chosen.
beats.ur:
Ek misal se poora clinical flow dekhein:
Source mein Daniel, 55 saal ke architect, ke shoulder mein hafton se stiffness hai. Active aur passive elevation dono limited, firm end-feel aur reduced joint glide milta hai; neck aur nerves ke checks clear hain. Hypomobile pattern ke mutabiq mobilization, stretching aur home exercises choose ki jati hain. Retest par elevation behtar hoti hai. Agar joint loose hota to stabilization exercise choose hoti. Yeh teaching scenario hai, universal treatment recommendation nahi.

text.en:
The mistakes I see most often:
• Treating the diagram instead of the examination.
• Mobilizing a hypermobile joint.
• Skipping the retest.
**Myth to drop:** 'One perfect glide fixes every stiff joint.' Joint findings and symptom responses are more variable than that.
text.ur: Examination ke bajaye diagram ko follow karna; hypermobile joint mobilize karna; aur retest skip karna.

text.en:
The Paris approach is a reasoning framework, not one treatment. Its components (manual therapy plus exercise) have varying evidence depending on the condition.
Joint mobilization can be an adjunct for selected musculoskeletal presentations; research on joint mobilization in general should not be mislabeled as proof for every Paris-branded protocol.
text.ur: Examine karein, classify karein, finding ke mutabiq treatment dein aur retest karein. Paris approach reasoning framework hai, ek single treatment nahi. Is ke components ki evidence condition ke mutabiq mukhtalif hoti hai.
